extracted.intended_audience: aspiring sports reporters, journalism students, and early-career sports journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide enumerating the core skills, qualities, and professional standards a sports reporter needs to produce accurate, engaging, and ethical coverage across platforms. Useful for training, self-assessment, and job preparation in sports journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: A deep passion for sports
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine passion for sports is the single most important quality; it fuels long hours, persistence, creativity, and the ability to spot story angles a casual observer would miss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passion drives the late nights covering games, early mornings chasing interviews, and constant attention to scores, trades, injuries, and controversies. It also translates into credibility with athletes, coaches, and fans; reporters who truly love the sport pick up on stories and angles others miss. Without it sports reporting becomes transactional and audiences sense the disconnect.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth knowledge of sports rules and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough understanding of the rules, regulations, and governance structures of the sport covered (laws of the game, league structures, anti-doping rules, transfer regulations, roles of governing bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy depends on knowing what constitutes an offside, a DRS review, or a salary cap violation. Familiarity with bodies like FIFA, ICC, IOC matters. Build expertise through study, attending matches, and tracking rule/policy changes; many ex-athletes transition because they already have this foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic integrity in sports
rubrics_metrics.description: Separating personal opinion from factual reporting and adhering to core journalistic ethics (seek truth, minimize harm, act independently, be accountable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrity starts with knowing the facts thoroughly and reporting them impartially. Follow frameworks like the Society of Professional Journalists’ Code of Ethics: verify claims before publishing, issue corrections promptly, and avoid letting fandom or personal bias shape reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong writing and communication skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to write clearly, concisely, and compellingly across story lengths—from 500-word match reports to long-form features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the action and drama of a game and translate it into copy readers understand and feel. Clarity, tight prose, and an engaging narrative voice are essential for both short deadline copy and in-depth features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to process complex events quickly and produce clean, engaging copy on tight deadlines (e.g., filing match reports within minutes of a game's end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the most newsworthy angle fast, prioritize facts, and write accurate copy under time constraints. Develop routines and templates for quick fact-checking and rapid drafting to reduce errors when speed is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting to multiple platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to tailor reporting and storytelling for television, radio, websites, social media, podcasts, and other platforms, each requiring different styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tweet requires brevity and punch; a TV package needs strong visuals and spoken narrative; a podcast thrives on conversational analysis. Versatility across platforms increases value to a newsroom and requires adjusting tone, length, and multimedia elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting sharp, relevant interviews with athletes, coaches, officials, and analysts—often in high-pressure environments like post-match press conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make subjects comfortable, ask focused follow-ups, extract meaningful quotes, and be prepared with background knowledge. Employers expect solid presenting and interviewing abilities; preparation and listening are key to getting new information rather than rehearsed lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and storytelling ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding the human angle and crafting a compelling narrative that goes beyond numbers and scores to resonate emotionally with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fresh angles, data visualization, and multimedia (text, video, audio, infographics) to create memorable stories. Creativity can mean offering new perspectives on commonly covered events or combining formats (e.g., a TikTok clip plus an in-depth feature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and commitment to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifying every statistic, quote, name, and claim to maintain credibility; checking context and explaining why events matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check statistics and quotes, rely on reliable sources, verify claims before publishing, and issue corrections when necessary. Accuracy also involves contextualizing events with history and analysis to help audiences understand significance. Follow ethical codes (e.g., SPJ) emphasizing truth, accountability, and minimizing harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building and maintaining relationships in the sports community
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing trust with athletes, coaches, agents, administrators, and other insiders to gain access to exclusive information and story leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationships come from consistent professionalism and fairness; they yield off-the-record insights, early tips, and behind-the-scenes access. Maintain boundaries to protect independence—getting too close can compromise coverage, particularly during controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The practical outcome of good relationship-building—better access to sources and information grounded in earned trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust leads to exclusive interviews and tips; however, guard against conflicts of interest and blurred lines (e.g., gifts, favours). Prioritize the audience and independence over personal relationships when reporting on sensitive matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking across the ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a broad network beyond players and coaches, including administrators, medical staff, agents, legal experts, statisticians, and fellow journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A diverse network provides multiple sources for different stories—match reports, investigative features, governance issues. Cultivate contacts across roles to cross-check information and deepen reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical and research skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting data, advanced metrics, and performance analytics to explain patterns, tactical shifts, and trends as part of data-driven journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand metrics like expected goals (xG) or WAR, use data visualization tools, and combine numbers with narrative. Research skills also apply to investigative work (doping, financial irregularities, governance failures) and to thorough pre-interview preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability and working under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding quickly to unpredictable events (injuries, delays, controversial decisions) and adjusting story angles and production in real time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to file updates, change plans, and learn new technical tools (live-blogging, video editing, social analytics). Willingness to experiment with formats and technologies helps reporters stay relevant as the media landscape evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding bias and sensationalism, respecting confidentiality and privacy, distinguishing news from opinion, and preventing conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality for sensitive stories, respect athletes’ privacy on personal matters, avoid accepting gifts/favours from teams, and be culturally sensitive—avoid stereotypes and racially insensitive language. Ethical reporting sustains credibility and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Mindfulness about avoiding stereotypes, racial bias, or culturally insensitive language in global sports coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for fair representation of diverse athletes and teams; contextualize cultural references and consult knowledgeable sources to avoid mischaracterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital and social media proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Using social platforms and digital tools for newsgathering, audience engagement, and content production (X, Instagram, YouTube, CMS, video/audio editing, basic graphic design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor social media for breaking news, engage with fans and sources, and drive traffic to long-form work. Beware the risk of sharing unverified rumours—verification is critical when speed and reach are high. Technical skills in production tools increase versatility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical stamina and mental resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Endurance for long hours, travel, odd schedules, and the emotional demands of the beat (criticism, hostile environments, tragic events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major tournaments may require filing multiple stories daily for extended periods. Maintain composure and professionalism under pressure; develop coping strategies for criticism and emotionally taxing assignments to sustain a long career.
